end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from source to consumer.
Identified fuel use and pollution as linked to transporting food.
Compared local May mangoes with imported or December mangoes.
Suggested local, seasonal food reduces distance, fuel, pollution, and storage time.
Teach-back was not passed; imported food was still linked with better taste or nutrition.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised tracing where foods come from, defining food miles, and explaining links with fuel, pollution, freshness, and storage. They used the local May mango example to identify lower food miles, lower cost, seasonal freshness, and support for local farmers. They continued to mix up imported food with better taste or extra vitamins, and this was not corrected by the last response. At home, ask them to compare two foods by distance travelled, fuel or storage needs, and one limit of choosing local food.
